passage:
Nilesh: You looked so calm last month. How did you handle the report, your sister's wedding shopping and the volunteering all at once?
Gargi: Honestly, I nearly didn't. On a Sunday I took a page and wrote everything I'd promised, all eight things. I stared at it. Then I told the people who needed to know: the volunteering group got “I'll skip two weeks”, my sister got “Saturdays only for the shopping”, and my manager got the report date confirmed. Then I worked through them in order, single-mindedly. It was a bit awkward saying it aloud. But nobody was angry, and nothing collapsed silently, which is what I was scared of.

qa.q: How many things did Gargi write on the page?
qa.a: Gargi wrote down all eight things, everything promised.

qa.q: What did Gargi feel about telling people what would be delayed?
qa.a: Gargi felt awkward saying it aloud, and was scared that things would collapse silently, but nobody was angry.

qa.q: What did Gargi tell the sister and the volunteering group?
qa.a: Gargi told the sister that shopping would be on Saturdays only, and told the volunteering group that Gargi would skip two weeks.

qa.q: What might Nilesh be thinking as Gargi explains?
qa.a: Nilesh is probably curious and impressed, and may be thinking of Nilesh's own overloaded list.

grounding: A wise person lists commitments, tells relevant people what will be delayed, and does each task in turn.

passage: I'm Mahima, and last Monday I saw Seema do something I'd never seen anyone do. Seema had four projects, a training day and a family function that week. Instead of frowning at all of them, Seema took a sticky note, wrote them in order and crossed off one that could wait. Then Seema walked to the manager's desk and said, “The vendor review will move to next Wednesday. Everything else stays.” A call went to the training coordinator too, and a message to a cousin about the function. After that Seema worked on one file only, phone face down. I can't say how Seema felt, but the day looked calmer than mine.

qa.q: Which task did Seema move to next Wednesday?
qa.a: Seema moved the vendor review to next Wednesday.

qa.q: How does Mahima think Seema felt that day?
qa.a: Mahima cannot be sure, but Seema looked calmer, and probably felt steadier after telling people the truth about what would wait.

qa.q: What steps did Seema take before working on a single file?
qa.a: Seema wrote the commitments in order, crossed one off, told the manager, the training coordinator and a cousin, and then put the phone face down.

qa.q: How might the manager have felt hearing that the vendor review would move?
qa.a: The manager may feel a little surprised, but honest notice at once lets the manager plan, which is better than silent failing.

grounding: A wise person lists commitments, tells relevant people what will be delayed and does each task in turn.
